entry.title: IceCube Nobel Prize
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced on 6 October that the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics goes to Francis Halzen, IceCube principal investigator, for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. At the South Pole, the entire station gathered at the IceCube Lab for a group photo on hearing the news. Halzen has also been interviewed on the importance of neutrino research and scientific collaboration.

entry.title: P-ONE photomultipliers
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. P-ONE is a planned cubic-kilometre-scale neutrino telescope for the Pacific Ocean, using Ocean Networks Canada deep-sea infrastructure. A new paper characterises all 320 3-inch R14374-10 photomultiplier tubes for the first detector line before deployment, and reports that all of them satisfy the specified acceptance criteria.

entry.title: IceCube transient searches
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. An analysis of 14 years of public IceCube muon-track data looked for neutrinos from 27 fast X-ray transients detected by Einstein Probe. It found no statistically significant excess, and the largest test statistic, for EP240801a, has a local p-value of 0.04. The authors therefore set 90% confidence level upper limits on the muon-neutrino flux.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper calculates neutrino emissivity from Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, motivated by the possible presence of Δ isobars in dense cores. It addresses a contribution to neutrino cooling that, according to the abstract, had not been explicitly determined before. It is relevant for anyone modelling neutron-star thermal evolution.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem: open two-flavour neutrino oscillations with evolution covariant under rotati
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem: open two-flavour neutrino oscillations with evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane are exactly blind to a Majorana phase. It also shows that a rate anisotropy in the environment can supply a phase reference. This defines when decoherence could make a Majorana phase observable in oscillations.

entry.title: The paper uses solar neutrino data from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande to constrain an ultralight vector b
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper uses solar neutrino data from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande to constrain an ultralight vector boson in the gauged L_μ − L_τ model. The boson, through kinetic mixing with the photon, would generate a matter potential in the Sun that modifies MSW oscillations. It also considers prospects for JUNO and XLZD.

entry.title: The paper computes the two-neutrino double-beta decay rate without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepto
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the two-neutrino double-beta decay rate without decoupling nuclear structure from the lepton kinematics, and compares it with closure, non-closure and Taylor-expansion approximations for 82Se and 136Xe. It reports deviations in both the rates and the electron spectra from those traditional methods. This is relevant to the interpretation of double-beta decay spectra.

entry.title: The paper studies thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, in which neutrino masses arise f
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, in which neutrino masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model gives sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale. The authors argue that leptogenesis here differs from canonical seesaw leptogenesis.

entry.title: The paper investigates two-photon neutrino interactions at a future muon collider, using dimension-7 effective
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper investigates two-photon neutrino interactions at a future muon collider, using dimension-7 effective operators and the process μ⁻γ → μ⁻νν̄ with a Weizsäcker–Williams photon. It uses MadGraph5_aMC@NLO and PYTHIA 8 to simulate signal and background. It probes neutrino electromagnetic properties in a way complementary to low-energy experiments.
